subject: Values Aligned Local Investment Ordinance Debate
overview: The Council advanced several administrative measures and an emergency facade restoration for the Medford Armory. Public testimony was dominated by a controversial proposal for ethical investment standards and concerns over labor practices in city schools.

items.title: Ceremonial resolutions, records, and donations
items.summary: The Council approved condolences for the family of Brian Deeb Hilliard, recognized the Tufts University Government and Community Relations Team, approved meeting records, and accepted a $500 donation from Boston Proud Corp.

items.title: Litigation settlement report
items.summary: Approved a Committee of the Whole report regarding the settlement of litigation in the matter of Aleesha Nunley Benjamin versus the City of Medford.

items.title: Tabling of zoning and investment ordinances
items.summary: Tabled proposed amendments to the Other Corridors zoning districts and the local investments ordinance until the next regular meeting.

items.title: Civil Project Manager personnel amendment
items.summary: Approved a first reading of an ordinance amendment to add a non-union Civil Project Manager position to the engineering division.

items.title: Medford Square and West Medford Square zoning
items.summary: Continued a public hearing on proposed zoning amendments for the Medford Square and West Medford Square districts to September 9, 2025.

items.title: Obie's Auto Service and Collision license petition
items.summary: Approved a Class 2 auto dealer license for Obie's Auto Service and Collision LLC, subject to 30, 60, and 90-day reviews to monitor potential neighborhood parking impacts.

items.title: Public testimony: Shade tree removal
items.summary: Heard from a Walcott Street resident seeking a hearing for the removal of a public shade tree; a response from the DPW Commissioner was read stating the permit was denied by the tree warden.

items.title: Public testimony: Janitorial labor dispute
items.summary: Representatives from SEIU 32BJ testified regarding a transition to a non-union cleaning contractor at Medford High School and the alleged refusal to hire former union staff.

items.title: Values Aligned Local Investment Ordinance
items.summary: Conducted a lengthy public hearing where dozens of residents debated an ethical investment ordinance, with critics arguing it unfairly targets Israel and endangers Jewish residents, while supporters characterized it as a necessary stance against human rights violations and fossil fuels.

items.title: Rodent infestation update
items.summary: Referred a resolution concerning rat infestations in the Wellington and Glenwood neighborhoods to the Committee of the Whole for a meeting with the Health Department and pest control vendors.

items.title: Good Landlord Tax Credit analysis
items.summary: Approved a request for legal and financial opinions regarding the potential local implementation of a tax credit for landlords who offer below-market rates in small residential properties.

items.title: Food truck permits
items.summary: Approved four food truck permits for the Medford Square Fest events occurring at the Clippership Pop-Up Park in August.

items.title: CPA appropriation: Medford Armory facade
items.summary: Approved a $37,280 Community Preservation Act appropriation for emergency facade restoration at the Medford Armory building.
